headline: No votes taken on rent control changes, inclusionary zoning, or a Bloomberg housing program.
summary: Staff gave the third-quarter rent control report. Corporation Counsel reviewed proposed changes to strengthen rent control enforcement, and two stakeholders spoke on inclusionary zoning. The Bloomberg housing program was also discussed, and no votes were taken.
discussion: Rent control definitions: Members discussed proposed changes to definitions in the rent control ordinance, including housing services, dwelling units, and parking. Some said housing services needs a clearer definition, while others said the rent board should keep its discretion.

Rent control enforcement penalties: Members asked how a proposed fine schedule and the remedy for substantial non-compliance would work. Staff said the fine amounts were examples only, and members said the figures need more review.

Inclusionary zoning review: Two stakeholders urged the committee to bring in outside housing policy experts before making changes. They said the voter-approved policy has increased affordable units and suggested a stakeholder process like the 1987 waterfront review.
Bloomberg housing program: Members asked about a possible two-year technical assistance offer of up to $750,000. Staff will review the program materials and bring back options before any decision.
